brief: Goldman's broad-based AI basket has fallen 20% in five sessions, towards the lower end of past unwind episodes, and the SOX has posted its first eight-day losing streak since September 2015 (down more than 15% over the stretch), while systematic multi-strategy funds had a 2.2 sigma down day (though they remain up 20% YTD). The note frames this as either a positioning unwind or the start of something more fundamental, citing two concerns: scrutiny of AI data centers' high-yield debt financing model, and Chinese hardware exports up about 36% year-over-year, which threatens the US hardware bottleneck thesis. Against that, the NDX forward P/E has fallen to about 21x, its lowest since the 2023 AI cycle began, and the index is testing its trendline from the March lows, seen as a potentially supportive setup into earnings season. Data-center capex estimates for 2027 keep rising despite higher rates, and AI financing costs remain not excessive versus the rest of the credit stack, though the gap widens further out the curve. Goldman's desk likes buying the non-AI basket (SPXXAI), expecting AI/non-AI dispersion to narrow as headline risk catches up with pricing.
